framing_issues.text: Georgia Power and GIPL say real-time customers should carry only costs they can change
framing_issues.issue: Misattribution. GIPL is credited with a principle its own testimony contradicts: GIPL wants real-time load to carry pipeline (FT), coal-related and overhead costs (P-096, P-101, P-156), which are fixed. Pairing GIPL with Georgia Power under one rationale misstates GIPL's position.

framing_issues.text: GAM witness Jonathan Ly said no part of real-time revenue should be credited against these fees
framing_issues.issue: Card 3 lists GAM under 'Who says it' for Georgia Power's winter-peak plan. GAM's quote (P-110) argues against any dedicated RTP credit for FT, while Georgia Power's plan books RTP revenue to fuel to cover new FT (P-127). This implies GAM backs a plan no passage shows it backing. 'No part' also drops GAM's 'specific'.

framing_issues.text: Resource Supply Management also filed testimony, on Sep 22.
framing_issues.issue: Names a party, and spells out 'RSM', with no passage support; P-002 shows only 'Jim Clarkson Direct Testimony'. The same name appears on line 28. This conflicts with the project rule against supplying speakers or sources.

framing_issues.text: the added money would have wiped out a $322 million shortfall
framing_issues.issue: Missing context. The $322 million and $1.35 figures are from page 7 of Staff's testimony, and the Oct 7 errata corrected 'page 7, line 9' (P-039). The caveat appears only in general terms (lines 120, 140), not where the figures are used, so readers may take possibly corrected numbers as current.

framing_issues.text: The big customers' own prices would not change.
framing_issues.issue: Unattributed reassurance in the 30-second version. It generalizes GIPL's statement about its own proposal (P-105), and real-time customers' baseline use is billed at standard rates (P-043) that the same bullet says could rise. Repeated on line 79.

framing_issues.text: Customers on standard rates keep paying the fixed fuel costs left out of the credit.
framing_issues.issue: Uneven attribution. PIA Staff's contested claim (P-063) is stated as fact under 'Who pays', while Georgia Power's opposing view (P-124) appears only as 'Georgia Power says' under 'What's uncertain'.

framing_issues.text: PIA Staff found Georgia Power could have absorbed the larger fuel credit
framing_issues.issue: Unequal verbs. 'Found' presents a party's conclusion as an established finding; other parties 'say' or 'said', and line 86 gives the same claim as 'PIA Staff says'.

framing_issues.text: whose members use large amounts of power
framing_issues.issue: Uneven context. Only GAM gets a cue about its members' stake. No parallel note is given for Georgia Power's earnings (P-091), GIPL's member congregations (P-093), or the outside consulting firms behind PIA Staff's and GAM's witnesses (P-160, P-161, P-108).

framing_issues.text: These are the four plans in the record.
framing_issues.issue: Overstates completeness. Option A is no party's plan (line 101), and RSM's testimony was not read, so these are not 'the four plans in the record'.

framing_issues.text: None of the four parties whose testimony we archived asks to keep it unchanged.
framing_issues.issue: Understates GAM, whose testimony comes closest to defending today's method (P-110, P-111) and accepts a change only conditionally. 'Four parties whose testimony we archived' is also inaccurate: five filed, and RSM's was archived but not read.

framing_issues.text: GAM says either of Georgia Power's options would work.
framing_issues.issue: Drops GAM's condition ('Should the Commission find... should be modified', P-111). It makes GAM read as a supporter of Option B, and 'options' covers only the two take-or-pay choices, not the pipeline plan.

framing_issues.text: "Supported" means the case record or a party's own figures back the claim.
framing_issues.issue: Label rule lets one party's own estimate earn 'Supported'; card 2's header rests on PIA Staff's estimate from data Staff calls incomplete. Readers may take the label as independent confirmation.

framing_issues.text: You can speak at the hearing as a public witness
framing_issues.issue: Practical risk. No passage confirms public witnesses will be heard at the Nov 12 rebuttal hearing (P-010); the page states it as a sure option here and on line 46.

framing_issues.text: Commissioners are elected.
framing_issues.issue: Missing context about accountability: Stan Wise holds his seat by appointment (P-033, P-034), and line 17's 'joined' hides that he served from 1994 to 2018.

framing_issues.text: using each group's share of winter peak growth to split the fees
framing_issues.issue: Jargon left unexplained. 'Winter peak' (coincident peak) splits, the 'transmission' split on line 124, and 'energy use' splits are the core of cards 3 and 4, but the page never says in plain words what each means or who pays more under each.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power's rebuttal says GIPL's witness switched to an energy-based split at a hearing.
framing_issues.issue: Omits the reason given in the same cited footnote: the change followed Georgia Power's data request responses filed after his testimony (P-155). Without it, the line echoes Georgia Power's 'unstable' framing (P-154).

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power asked the PSC to strike parts of GIPL's testimony.
framing_issues.issue: Procedural term 'strike' is not explained; P-134 means the parts would be excluded from the record and not considered. Also used on line 91.

framing_issues.text: associated interchange energy rate
framing_issues.issue: Technical term quoted without explanation.

framing_issues.text: an hourly average of the replacement fuel cost
framing_issues.issue: 'Replacement fuel cost' is unexplained, and dropping 'marginal' blurs the marginal-versus-average distinction the case turns on (P-048, P-052).

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power estimates $100 million more in base rates would raise a typical home's bill a bit more
framing_issues.issue: Placed under 'What supports it' for GAM, the pairing implies a net bill increase from shifting revenue. The base-side change is deferred to a regulatory asset and the next rate case (P-016), and base rates are frozen through 2028 (P-054), so the two effects are not simultaneous or necessarily equal.

framing_issues.text: GIPL said splitting by energy or by peak demand gives different results
framing_issues.issue: Listed as support for Staff's energy-based plan, but GIPL recommended a transmission-style (demand) split for new FT (P-104); its point is that the allocator matters, not that energy is right.

framing_issues.text: Should big customers on hourly prices help pay fuel costs that don't change with how much power they use?
framing_issues.issue: Slight presupposition that these customers do not already help pay; Georgia Power says they do through base-side revenue (P-124). A neutral form: 'Should part of these fixed fuel costs be counted against real-time payments?'

framing_issues.text: Some big businesses, including data centers
framing_issues.issue: Leads with data centers, a framing taken from GIPL's testimony about subsidy concerns (P-097). The program covers about 2,470 commercial and industrial customers from 250 kW up (P-044).

framing_issues.text: PIA Staff and other parties asked for the review
framing_issues.issue: Omits that Georgia Power 'supported and agreed to this subsequent review' (P-053), which could suggest the company resisted it.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power says Option 1 keeps real-time pricing
framing_issues.issue: Category mismatch. A rate-design argument sits under 'Who benefits', while Options C and D use that field for customer effects.
